claim: Vaduz Castle is the private residence of the Princely Family and its interior is closed to the public, but the grounds are accessible via a 15-minute uphill footpath behind the Landesmuseum, opened to visitors only on August 15 (National Day).
quote: Vaduz Castle - Official tourism website of the Principality of Liechtenstein. The castle serves as the private residence of the Princely Family of Liechtenstein and the interior is not open to the public.

claim: The Liechtensteinisches Landesmuseum (Städtle 43, Vaduz) opens Tue-Sun 10am-5pm (Wed to 8pm), CHF 10 adult, with a combo ticket including the Treasure Chamber for CHF 13.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday 10 am to 5 pm. Wednesday 10 am to 8 pm. Combo ticket covers both the National Museum and Treasure Chamber. Regular CHF 13.

claim: The Schatzkammer (Treasure Chamber) is open daily 10am-5pm and holds princely treasures from five centuries including Fabergé eggs (Apple Blossom Egg), Apollo 11/17 moon rocks, a replica of the Princely Hat, and a perpetual calendar made for Emperor Rudolf II.
quote: Open daily, 10 am to 5 pm. Treasures from five centuries that is unique in the Alpine region. Fabergé eggs and moon rocks from the Apollo 11 (1969) and Apollo 17 (1972) manned lunar missions.

claim: Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein (Städtle 32, Vaduz) is closed Mondays, open Tue-Sun 10am-5pm (Thu to 8pm), CHF 12-15 adult, with free admission every Wednesday and August 15.
quote: Closed on Mondays, open Tuesday-Wednesday from 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Thursday from 10:00 AM - 8:00 PM. Entry fees are CHF 12-15 for adults. Every Wednesday and on August 15th admission is free.

claim: The Hofkellerei des Fürsten von Liechtenstein in Vaduz runs public tastings Mon-Sat at 15:00 including a champagne reception, vineyard/cellar tour and six wines (~60-90 minutes); groups under 6 need no booking, larger groups must email office@hofkellerei.li.
quote: The tasting includes a champagne reception, a guided tour of the vineyard and cellar and a tasting of six selected wines. It takes place from Monday to Saturday at 15:00, and the event lasts around 60 to 90 minutes.

claim: The Princely Winery's Herawingert vineyard in Vaduz spans four hectares with southwest exposure and a mild foehn climate, considered one of the best vineyards in the Rhine Valley.
quote: With its four hectares of vineyards, Herawingert is one of the best vineyards in the Rhine Valley due to its south-western exposure and mild foehn climate.

claim: The Liechtenstein Center tourist office (Städtle 39, Vaduz) sells the novelty souvenir passport stamp for CHF 3 / EUR 3.30 and is open seven days a week.
quote: Souvenir stamp: CHF 3 / EUR 3.30 (complimentary for ALL INCLUSIVE Adventure Pass holders). Expert information available seven days a week.

claim: The Liechtenstein-Weg (Liechtenstein Trail) is a 75 km route through all 11 municipalities, divided into five official stages, accompanied by the LIstory app delivering cultural/historical commentary, with luggage transport bookable.
quote: 75 km of exciting stories, sights and magnificent views. The LIstory app accompanies visitors with exciting stories and insights into the country's culture and history.

claim: The Fürstensteig is a 5.9 km circular alpine hike (~2h45, 478 m ascent, max 1929 m) starting at Alp Gaflei, with exposed sections secured by wire ropes; surefootedness and a head for heights required; reach the trailhead via Liechtenstein Bus to Gaflei, Kurhaus.
quote: Distance: 5.9 km. Duration: 2 hours 45 minutes. Elevation Gain/Loss: 478m ascent, 481m descent. The Fürstensteig requires surefootedness and a head for heights. Exposed sections secured with wire ropes.

claim: The Liechtensteinisches PostMuseum in the Englanderbau, Vaduz, is open daily 10am-5pm with free admission, showing every stamp issued since 1912.
quote: Postmuseum Vaduz, established in 1936, is dedicated to the history of Liechtenstein's postal service and philately. Located in the Englanderbau in Vaduz. Free admission. Daily 10 am to 5 pm.

claim: From Bad Ragaz to Vaduz is roughly 13 miles; train to Schaan-Vaduz via Sargans runs hourly in ~16 minutes, while LIEmobil bus 11 from Sargans Bahnhof to Vaduz Post departs every 30 minutes (~32 min), and driving takes about 13 minutes.
quote: The distance between Bad Ragaz and Vaduz is 13 miles. Verkehrsbetrieb Liechtensteinmobil operates a bus from Sargans, Bahnhof to Vaduz, Post every 30 minutes, and the journey takes 32 min.

claim: LIEmobil operates the Liechtenstein public bus network; line 11 is the main Sargans Bahnhof - Vaduz - Schaan - Buchs/Feldkirch backbone, integrated with Swiss rail tickets and the Swiss Travel Pass.
quote: Timetable, Operation notices, News. LIEmobil 11 bus Route Map - Sargans Bahnhof.

claim: The Liechtenstein Trail's five stages run 8.5-19.6 km per day; stage 2 from Triesenberg passes Schalun Castle ruins and Vaduz Castle, and stage 3 leaves Vaduz past the Court Winery and Roman ruins to Schaan.
quote: Following the official five stages will see you walking a minimum of 8.5 and maximum of 19.6 kilometres per day. Stage 2 leads from Triesenberg via the historic Prufatscheng farmstead past the majestic Vaduz Castle.
